meta.verification_method: Each published claim is checked against the linked public source text or structured record. Source conflicts, moving rankings and unavailable pre-event statistics are kept visible; see data/research-ledger.json and the Verified List page.
meta.notes: Counter-Strike rosters and rankings change frequently. Ranking figures are snapshots with exact dates. Live Valve (VRS) rankings on HLTV differ from Valve's last published snapshot; both are cited where relevant.
meta.verification_passes: Two passes on Sept 23, 2026 (first build + 20 new ledger entries in the second pass). Ledger: data/research-ledger.json (40 entries).

tournament.name: Thunderpick World Championship 2026 (TWC 2026)
tournament.venue: BLAST Studios Malta (Attard, Malta per Liquipedia; 'BLAST Studios Malta' per official release)
tournament.prize_split: 50% players / 50% club share (per HLTV event page)

format.group_stage: Two double-elimination (GSL) groups of 4; all matches Bo3; top 2 of each group advance
format.playoffs: Single-elimination bracket; Bo3 except Bo5 Grand Final; third-place decider match played

previous_winners.2024: The MongolZ (3-1 vs HEROIC in Berlin, Nov 3, 2024; 16 teams, $850,000 total; 3DMAX 3rd)
previous_winners.2025: FURIA (reverse sweep 3-2 vs NAVI in Malta; KSCERATO Grand Final MVP; NAVI $150k, MongolZ $70k, Aurora $50k)

tournament.context: One of the last VRS point opportunities before the PGL Major Singapore 2026 (Nov 25 - Dec 13); PGL Masters Bucharest (Oct 24-31) follows one week after TWC.

finals_week_schedule.travel_and_accommodation: TWC covers T&A for up to 7 persons per team

tournament.twc_2025_viewership: Set the series record: +62% over the 2024 finals (official PR, Oct 27, 2025)
tournament.note_dates: The official site headline "12-19 October" is the full Finals week (arrival Oct 12 through departure Oct 19); match days are Oct 14-18. This resolves the earlier flag about HLTV's "October 12-19" plan.

circuit_2026.note: M80 beat Wildcard 2-0 (16-14 Dust2, 13-10 Inferno) in the final; only two of seven playoff series were played - the rest were forfeits by teams unable to field eligible lineups (Liquipedia logs the forfeits).
Winner played as VRSDelivery in the final (May 31); the org renamed to DragonClaw on May 30, 2026 (Liquipedia). TDK (nafany, Ax1Le) finished 2nd.
Imperial won 2-0 (8-4 first halves on both Dust2 and Inferno); their 4-0 start after signing saadzin from Legacy.
CYBERSHOKE (PARIVISION loanee nota) and ex-1win shared 3rd-4th.

valve_vrs_global_2026_08_03_invite_basis.note: August 3, 2026 VRS snapshot was the basis for the 7 direct Finals invites; Virtus.pro qualified via the Global Qualifier instead.

hltv_live_valve_ranking_2026_09_23.note: HLTV's continuously-updated live implementation of the Valve ranking, read from each team's badge on the TWC 2026 event page on Sept 23, 2026. Differs from Valve's last published snapshot (Sept 7) because it includes results after that date (e.g., Legacy's FISSURE Playground 3 title).

irregularities.issue: Prize pool figures differ across sources
irregularities.detail: Official Thunderpick/PRNewswire: $1,115,000 total circuit with $1,000,000 for the Malta Finals. EGamersWorld/Strafe/escharts list the Finals at $500,000, and GosuGamers lists $615,000. The $500,000 figure may reflect only the club share of the $1M (HLTV splits it as $500k player share / $500k club share); GosuGamers' $615,000 matches no official figure.
irregularities.resolution: Site uses the official $1,000,000 Finals / $1,115,000 circuit figures.

irregularities.detail: Official releases say 'BLAST Studios Malta' (one PR dateline: Ta' Qali). Liquipedia lists 'BLAST Arena Studios, Attard'. Some outlets wrote 'Valletta'. All refer to the same BLAST studio venue in Malta.
irregularities.resolution: Site uses 'BLAST Studios, Malta (Attard per Liquipedia)'.

irregularities.detail: HLTV's Dec 11, 2025 article said the LAN finals would be 'October 12-19'. Final official dates are October 14-18, 2026.
irregularities.resolution: Site uses Oct 14-18 (Liquipedia, HLTV event page, official PR). Resolved further: the official site's 'Finals 2026: 12-19 October' is the arrival-through-departure window (arrival Oct 12, media day Oct 13, groups Oct 14-16, playoffs Oct 17-18, departure Oct 19) - match days remain Oct 14-18.

irregularities.detail: PRNewswire (Sept 16) listed e.g. 'Legacy #3, Falcons #4, FURIA #8'; esportbet wrote 'Falcons #2, FURIA #4'. These mix ranking systems/dates (HLTV weekly vs Valve VRS snapshots vs HLTV's live Valve ranking). Example: Legacy is #6 on HLTV's Sept 21 ranking, #6 on Valve's Sept 7 VRS snapshot, but #2 on HLTV's live Valve ranking badge (Sept 23). Verified on Sept 23: the HLTV event page badges carry both ranks - e.g., Legacy shows #6 (HLTV weekly) and #2 (live Valve); FURIA #4 / #8; Falcons #5 / #5; BetBoom #15 / #10; 9z #16 / #13; PARIVISION #19 / #23; VP #50 / #43.
irregularities.resolution: Site always labels which system and which date: HLTV World Ranking (Sept 21) and Valve VRS official snapshots (Aug 3 invite basis; Sept 7 latest published).

irregularities.detail: Valve's Aug 3 VRS snapshot lists rosters that were already outdated (FL4MUS on BetBoom, saadzin on Legacy, HObbit+slaxejezzz on PARIVISION). The TWC Finals rosters reflect the actual, current lineups.

As of the second verification pass on Sept 23, 2026, group placements and the day-by-day schedule remain TBD on Liquipedia and HLTV; only the finals-week structure (arrival/media/group/playoff days) is published on the official site.
irregularities.resolution: Marked as pending; to be updated in a future session.

irregularities.issue: No outright winner odds available at research time
irregularities.detail: esportbet's dedicated TWC betting hub still showed no TWC odds at the Sept 23 second-pass check; Thunderpick (title sponsor) will offer markets per their official site.
irregularities.resolution: Betting guide provides verified form/H2H data and a framework instead of live odds; links provided for manual odds checks.

irregularities.detail: 9z's and PARIVISION's official in-game-leader designations are not explicitly stated in the sources gathered (max and Jame are the veteran leaders historically associated with calling)
irregularities.resolution: Explicitly labeled 'not officially labeled' on the Players page rather than asserted

irregularities.issue: EU Series 1 winner appears under two names
irregularities.detail: Hotspawn's final report (May 31) names VRSDelivery; HLTV's prize list names DragonClaw. Liquipedia documents the rename on May 30, 2026 - same team. A related but separate item: Liquipedia logs DragonClaw's June 2 disqualification from European Pro League Series 7 pending an organizer investigation into 'suspicious activity' (a different event, not TWC).
irregularities.resolution: Site names DragonClaw (as VRSDelivery) with the rename explained; the EPL investigation is flagged as outside TWC scope.

irregularities.detail: The 2025-26 pre-karrigan period is sometimes summarized as '7 grand finals, 1 title'. The precise, source-backed read: Falcons won PGL Bucharest 2025 (Apr 13, with degster) BEFORE m0NESY joined; with m0NESY they then lost seven straight finals (IEM Melbourne, BLAST Rivals Spring 2025, EWC 2025, ESL Pro League S22, IEM Chengdu 2025, BLAST Rivals Fall 2025, BLAST Bounty Winter 2026).
irregularities.resolution: Site states the precise sequence instead of a bare count.

limitations: Match/outright odds for TWC 2026 were still not published at the second-pass check (Sept 23, 2026) - betting analysis is framework + verified form data, not live prices.
Group draw and day-by-day schedule for the Finals are not yet published (only the finals-week structure is).
HLTV player statistics for the Finals will only exist after the event; linked for post-event review.
Head-to-head data now covers all four 2026 FURIA-Falcons meetings plus the 2025 BLAST Rivals final, but full H2H scraping (all 28 pairings, all maps) is future work.
Some primary sources are X/Twitter posts (e.g., PARIVISION announcements) which may require login to view.
Rankings move weekly (HLTV) and per-snapshot (Valve); every rank figure on the site is labeled with system + date, including the live Valve ranks read from HLTV's event badges (Sept 23).
Roster news after Sept 23, 2026 is not captured and should be added in a follow-up pass before the event (Oct 14-18).
